questions.question: By volume, dry air is approximately:
Why are the standard percentages always quoted for DRY air?
options: Because water vapour is a VARIABLE component, ranging from almost nothing to about 4%, so including it would make the figures unstable
Because instruments cannot measure moist air
Because water vapour is not a gas

questions.question: The main role of nitrogen in the atmosphere is to:
options: DILUTE oxygen so combustion proceeds at a controllable rate, and supply the raw material that fixing bacteria convert for plant proteins

questions.question: Dust and other aerosols matter to weather mainly because they:
options: Act as CONDENSATION NUCLEI — surfaces for water vapour to condense onto, without which raindrops struggle to form

subtopics.title: The Four Layers — Structure by Temperature

questions.question: The atmosphere is divided into layers on the basis of:
options: The direction in which temperature changes with height

questions.question: Temperature FALLS with height in the troposphere at about 6,5 °C per 1 000 m because:
options: The sun is further away higher up
The atmosphere is heated FROM BELOW by long-wave radiation from the earth's surface, so distance from that source means cooler air

questions.question: Temperature RISES with height in the stratosphere because:
options: It is closer to the thermosphere
The ozone layer at 20–30 km absorbs ultraviolet radiation and converts it to heat

questions.question: The coldest part of the entire atmosphere, at about −90 °C, is the:
options: MESOPAUSE — the ceiling of the mesosphere, which has no ozone to warm it

subtopics.title: The Ozone Layer — Shield, Damage and Repair

questions.question: The ozone layer's function is to:
options: Absorb most incoming ultraviolet-B and ultraviolet-C radiation before it reaches the surface
Trap long-wave radiation leaving the earth

questions.question: CFCs are so damaging because they:
options: Are heavier than air and sink
Are chemically stable, so rain cannot wash them out and they drift into the stratosphere, where UV frees chlorine that destroys ozone CATALYTICALLY — one atom wrecking thousands of molecules

questions.question: Which effect of ozone depletion damages the base of the marine food web?
options: Damage to phytoplankton from extra ultraviolet radiation, with knock-on effects for fisheries

questions.question: The essential distinction the lesson insists on is that:
options: Both problems occur in the mesosphere
Ozone depletion is caused by carbon dioxide
The greenhouse effect thins the ozone layer
Ozone depletion lets radiation IN through the stratosphere; the greenhouse effect traps heat in the troposphere — different gases, layer and mechanism

subtopics.title: Why the Atmosphere Matters — and the Exam Method

questions.question: Without the natural greenhouse effect, the earth's average surface temperature would be about:
When a temperature-versus-height graph is supplied, the fastest way to identify every layer is to:
options: Work from the TURNING POINTS — each reversal is a pause (tropopause, stratopause, mesopause) and locates the layers
Measure the length of the line

questions.question: A complete description of any single layer must give:
options: Height range, direction of temperature change, the REASON for that change, and a distinguishing feature

questions.question: Ozone at ground level, produced by traffic and industry, is:
options: Part of the protective ozone layer
A POLLUTANT — the same molecule, opposite verdict, decided entirely by altitude

questions.question: In the bag of one hundred marbles standing for dry air:
options: 78 are nitrogen, 21 are oxygen, and one marble covers everything else

questions.question: Nitrogen is compared to the water you add to Oros concentrate because it:
options: DILUTES the oxygen, so fire burns steadily instead of tearing away

questions.question: Why does Durban air in February differ so much from Upington air in winter?
options: Different amounts of WATER VAPOUR — the ingredient that refuses to stay still, which is why the textbook figures say 'dry air'

subtopics.title: Four Storeys of One Strange Building

questions.question: On the ground floor — the troposphere — the 'heater' is:
options: The FLOOR itself: the ground absorbs sunshine and radiates warmth upward, so it gets colder as you climb

questions.question: Aeroplanes cruise in the bottom of the first floor — the stratosphere — because:
options: Warm air sitting on top of cool air acts as a lid: nothing rises, nothing churns, no clouds form — smooth flying above the weather

questions.question: The top floor — the thermosphere — reads thousands of degrees yet would freeze you because:
options: The thermometer is broken up there
There is almost no air there to touch you and pass the heat on

questions.question: Climbing the four storeys in order, the temperature pattern goes:
options: DOWN, UP, DOWN, UP — troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere

subtopics.title: The Sunscreen With a Hole In It

questions.question: Squeezed down to sea-level pressure, the whole ozone layer would be a film about:
options: Three millimetres thick — roughly the edge of a two-rand coin

questions.question: The 'master key' image describes chlorine because one chlorine atom:
options: Destroys thousands of ozone molecules one after another, because it is not used up in the reaction

questions.question: The practical habit named for ordinary households is to:
options: Have old fridges and air-conditioners DEGASSED by a technician rather than dumped on a scrapheap

questions.question: The Montreal Protocol is described as rare because:
options: It is the environmental problem the world genuinely fixed — CFCs were phased out and the layer is measurably healing
